title: The Circuit That Would Not Draw
eyebrow: Fixed, and it was not the camera

actions.fyi: Nothing is waiting on you. Everything is on main, read by a second agent, and the tests that were blocked are green.

content.label: What you would have seen
content.lead: Load a circuit with no car on it. Before, every surface was skipped as off-screen and the picture was empty. Now it opens at the start line.

before.caption: Before — not one surface in the frame

after.caption: After — the start line, where a car would be parked

blocks.label: Reading the picture
blocks.text: This is the view that paints each separate piece of the circuit its own colour, so a black frame means nothing at all was drawn.

content.label: The number that gave it away
content.lead: How much of the circuit gets skipped as off-screen, from three very different camera positions.

rows: Before — 14 m from the start line

blocks.label: Why that is the answer
blocks.text: A count of what is off-screen that does not move when the camera moves cannot be a count of what is off-screen.

content.label: Two wrong answers first
content.lead: The obvious reading was a badly aimed camera. It was wrong twice, and that is what found the real fault.

rows.title: Frame the whole circuit
rows.note: Put the camera 38 km back, far enough to hold the entire venue. Identical numbers. Also revealing: a circuit's outer scenery spans 18 km, so framing all of it is never a usable view.

rows.title: Frame the start line
rows.note: Put the camera 14 m from where a car would be parked. Identical numbers again — and the same as sitting at the origin doing nothing.

rows.title: Load a car first, then the circuit
rows.note: Everything draws. That is the ablation that worked, and it pointed at what the car was quietly supplying: the camera itself.

content.label: What a second pair of eyes found
content.lead: An agent that never saw the work read both changes. It confirmed they land the result, and raised four points — three fixed here, one too big to absorb.

rows.title: The same mistake survived one line above the fix
rows.note: A circuit on its own was also being denied frame-to-frame smoothing, for the same reason. Fixed — and the new check has teeth: put the old condition back and 5573 pixels crawl forever instead of 13.

rows.title: Where an empty grid slot is was worked out twice
rows.note: The day a car-less slot gets settled onto the road, the camera would have kept framing the old spot. One place now decides it.

rows.title: A circuit with no start line still opened on nothing
rows.note: It now falls back to any marker the author shipped. A venue with none at all is written down as its own card.

rows.title: The default run still does not exercise the fixed path
rows.note: Because a car is always loaded first and nothing can unload it — the app has no way to take a car out of a scene. That is a real missing capability, so it is its own job rather than a patch here.

blocks.label: Also checked and cleared
blocks.text: That a capture taken without a window keeps its own camera, that clearing a circuit still parks a car at the studio origin, that nothing is newly cut off by distance, and that the existing check would have gone red before either fix.

rows.title: The sky
rows.note: About seventy old tests, the biggest single block left. Every one of them judges a picture of a circuit.

rows.title: Any measurement of a circuit at all
rows.note: Two of them came out green only because the run happened to load a car first. They now come out green on their own.

blocks.label: Nothing else moved
blocks.text: All twenty-four measurements green in one run of the app — twenty-three before, plus the new one that watches a circuit settle.

blocks.label: The point of the job
blocks.text: That middle number used to be 6 whenever the circuit happened to be measured first. It is now the same in every order, not merely green in every order.

decisions.title: Two failed attempts at a cause end the theory, they do not refine it
decisions.why: Guessing a third camera position would have cost the afternoon. The identical numbers were the finding.

decisions.title: The camera is sent to the renderer every frame, unconditionally
decisions.why: It is the frame's own state, not something a car brings with it. Any condition on it is another version of this same fault.

decisions.title: The related fault found alongside it was written down, not folded in
decisions.why: The same condition also switches off the picture's frame-to-frame smoothing for a car-less circuit. Real, separate, and on the board rather than smuggled into this fix.

decisions.title: A car-less circuit opens at the start line, framed as if a car were parked there
decisions.why: The obvious alternative — fit the whole venue on screen — puts the camera 38 km out, because a circuit's outer scenery spans 18 km. Falls back to any other place the circuit's author marked; a circuit that marked none is left alone rather than pointed somewhere arbitrary, and that gap is written down.

next.if_nothing: I start on the sky, which this unblocks.
